reasons: Classification is correct: Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work expressly including the bespoke 'Modifications', and the only Customer right (Section 2, read with the Authorized Locations limitation) is a non-exclusive, non-transferable use licence with no right to modify — this fails the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use/modify deliverables, so it is not an acceptable-fallback over-flag.

Second limb is also supported: no provision allocates ownership of Sparkling's data even though Garman converts and processes it under Section 4(b); confidentiality (Section 14) does not allocate ownership, so a data-ownership sentence is warranted under the rule's redline guidance.

Redline is directionally correct and additive: it leaves Garman's ownership of the Software platform and Improvements intact (permitted by the rule), adds a Customer Data / no-assignment sentence, and adds a licence back over the paid-for Modifications — the smallest edit that reaches the fallback, consistent with the 'add the licence-back' guidance.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position, and does not misstate what changed; deterministic checks confirm no assignment of Customer IP/data to Vendor remains.

Minor shortfall worth noting but not disqualifying: the granted licence covers 'use, modify and have modified ... for Sparkling's internal business purposes' and omits an express sublicensing right contemplated by the fallback; consider adding 'and sublicense (including to affiliates and service providers)' if the counterparty reopens the clause.
